baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: Warm start: the best model of run norman_control_replogle_w4_r0 (EXP_0198, visible 0.6423) is the starting point of this run.
The maximum prior_network edge weight between gene g and any target gene in perturbation p will predict g's response.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0032).

For pair perturbations, the difference between the sum of individual Replogle-derived target deltas and the Replogle-derived delta for the pair (if available) predicts the non-additive component of the response.
There is an optimal ridge alpha for the current best feature set plus replogle_target_delta_sum_e19 that improves performance. [sweep alpha_grid=1000]
For a pair perturbation A+B, the ratio of the sum of sign-flipped Replogle deltas for A and B to the sum of their absolute values adds predictive value.
For a pair perturbation A+B, the number of gene sets (from gene_sets) that contain both A and B is predictive of gene g's response.
For any perturbation p, a weighted average of sign-flipped Replogle deltas over p's target genes, where weights are the target's control mean expression, improves prediction of delta[p,g].
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0145).
Fine-tuning the ridge alpha in the range 100-1000 for the current best feature set can improve performance slightly. [sweep alpha_grid=1000]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=1000 for the best model (EXP_0178).
Fine-tuning the ridge penalty alpha over a wider range (e.g., 100-10000) will improve the current best model. [sweep alpha_grid=30000]
Add replogle_target_delta_sum_e19 to the best model (EXP_0211): it helped elsewhere and the best model lacks it.
The residual of the current best model captures systematic variation not explained by existing features; using it as an additional feature in a stacked model improves performance.
Removing the weak feature prior_network_edge_e8 from the current best model will not hurt and may improve generalization.
The shortest path length between the two targets of a pair perturbation in the PPI network is predictive of the perturbation's effect.
Removing replogle_target_delta_sum_e19 from the current best feature set does not reduce performance.
For a pair perturbation A+B, the number of transcription factors that regulate both A and B is a predictive feature of the pair's delta response.
The product of additive_singles_e15 and target_level_e11 captures gene-specific modulation of additive response by target expression level.
A PPI-proximity-weighted sum of sign-flipped Replogle deltas for targets predicts delta(p,g) better than the unweighted sum, because direct network neighbors of g are more informative.
A random projection of the concatenated control expression profiles of perturbation targets (for pairs, both targets) captures high-dimensional target state in a low-dimensional feature.
Drop target_level_e11 from the best model (EXP_0390) to test whether it still earns its place.
Applying a random Fourier feature mapping to the sign-flipped Replogle delta of the perturbation's targets (summed for pairs) captures nonlinear dose-response relationships.
Applying a random Fourier feature mapping to the additive single-gene prediction (additive_singles_e15) captures nonlinear interactions between genes and perturbations that linear ridge cannot.
A random projection of the PPI adjacency row for gene g captures network topology beyond simple distances.
The average control expression of shared PPI neighbors of a pair's targets is predictive of the pair's response.
For a pair perturbation A+B, the average sign-flipped Replogle delta of shared PPI neighbors of A and B is predictive of the pair's effect on gene g.
Product of sign-flipped Replogle delta of target and PPI distance to gene g captures distance-weighted external response.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0507).

most_useful_features.description: For a pair perturbation A+B, the deviation of the observed mean pair delta from the additive sum of the single-gene mean deltas of A and B; 0 for single perturbations.
Sum of sign-flipped Replogle CRISPRi deltas for the perturbation's target genes, broadcast to all genes.
Difference between Replogle pair delta and sum of single deltas (sign-flipped).
Gene-specific loading on top control-expression PCs, scaled by the perturbation's delta projection onto those PCs.
Element-wise product of additive_singles_e15 and target_level_e11.
Random Fourier feature mapping of additive_singles_e15 values.
PPI-proximity-weighted sum of sign-flipped Replogle2022_K562 deltas over a perturbation's target genes, weighting each target by 1/(1+distance_power*shortest_path_length(g,t)) in the PPI network.
Absolute value of the pair additivity residual (observed pair delta minus sum of single-gene deltas), broadcast to all genes.
For a pair perturbation A+B, ratio of the sum of sign-flipped Replogle deltas for A and B to the sum of their absolute values; for singles, the sign of the sign-flipped delta.
Product of sign-flipped Replogle delta of p's target(s) and shortest PPI distance from target to gene g.
